tb21_profile.skill: Diagnose from an unhelpful description that work exists but is unreachable from any branch, find it with reflog / fsck --lost-found / stash / dangling objects, and graft it onto master without losing anything
tb21_profile.domain: Git internals: HEAD, refs, reflog, the object store, detached HEAD, stash, merge
tb21_profile.task_form: Recover-and-repair with no pointer to the fault: inspect repository state, work out what happened, then restore it

verifier_notes: CORRECTION PASS (fix-team 03, verifier_strength.json now authoritative). software-engineering_20260503_182123_007 was kept out of final_top10 only by the stale FREE grade; it is `ok` and is now promoted to rank 8. I read its tests: six pytest cases that check the recovered src/feature.py defines calculate() returning a + b and also calculate_average, that test_feature.py carries `from feature import calculate` and test_add, and that the feature commits are reachable from git log --all - real content checks on recovered work, not file-exists. On merit it is the closest CalibForge item to this TB2.1 task: unreachable commits plus a deliberately noisy reflog, recovered and applied to the mainline branch, which is the TB2.1 task with the failure mode changed from detached HEAD to reset --hard. It displaces jelmer__dulwich-1578, the weakest of the ten here - a library-internals bug fix (porcelain.add writes an empty tree entry) that scores task_form 2 and teaches debugging dulwich rather than recovering a repository. SWE-Rebench therefore no longer appears in the final ten; that is the honest outcome, not an oversight. Retained from the original pass: tw_590222 (rebase onto master) and tw_590773 (cherry-pick) are TerminalWorld's most relevant entries; tw_590222 is also rehabilitated (now `strong`) but at overall 3 it states the goal without the diagnosis that is this task's whole difficulty, so it stays out. task_001466_99e645e3 is graded behavioral, not FREE; its tests run the artifact and assert on exit status, which the spec allows in final_top10, and its instruction is unusually specific about reflogs and dangling blobs.

notes: This is the clearest case in my five where the new corpora beat the v1 pool outright. Terminal-Lego-15k contains a dense cluster of git-recovery tasks and task_11565 ('Merge Commits Made in a Detached HEAD State onto Master') is effectively the same task as this TB2.1 item, with task_11606 a close second; five of the final ten are Terminal-Lego and all five are strong or better. CalibForge adds a second family - git repositories broken by disk failure, interrupted rebases or an over-eager gc - that is strongly verified and teaches object-store repair. SWE-Rebench turns out to be unexpectedly useful because it carries eight dulwich and six gitpython issues, i.e. debugging the guts of git itself; I filled its ten from those two libraries and one of them earns a final_top10 slot despite the task_form penalty. TMax's own shortlist was almost entirely irrelevant data-organisation chores - everything I used from TMax came from my own reflog/history searches. SWE-Smith has nothing on git at all; its ten are DVC and lockfile-merge tasks chosen as the least-bad adjacency and should be discounted at merge. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld both cover git but mostly as ordinary usage (stash, submodules, cherry-pick), not recovery.
